title: Selected generic components form a projective cover
statement: Let $e$ be a field [def-weil-field], $F/e$ a finite field extension [def-pc-field-extension], and $\ell$ a prime. Let $B$ be a nonempty proper finite-type $e$-scheme [def-weil-proper-morphism] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] that is a finite disjoint union of integral schemes [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Let $X$ be a normal projective $F$-scheme [def-kun-projective], viewed over $e$ by $\operatorname{Spec}F\to\operatorname{Spec}e$, and let $d:X\to B$ be an $e$-morphism. Normal means every local ring is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. For each generic point $b$ of $B$, suppose a generic point $c_b$ of $X$ is chosen with $d(c_b)=b$ and with finite residue-field extension of degree prime to $\ell$ [def-sc-generic-point] [def-weil-residue-field] [def-pc-field-tower]. Let $X^\circ$ be the union of the irreducible components of $X$ whose generic points are the chosen $c_b$ [def-weil-irreducible-components], with their open subscheme structures. Then $X^\circ$ is open and closed in $X$, is normal and projective over $F$, and meets the fibre over every generic point of $B$. The morphism $d|_{X^\circ}:X^\circ\to B$ is projective in both the finite-projective-space and projective-bundle conventions [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism], is surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism], and each of its generic points maps to a generic point of $B$ with finite residue degree prime to $\ell$. Its generic points are exactly the chosen $c_b$, with repetitions discarded. The omitted components need satisfy no degree condition.

source.place: ILO Expose X 2.3 Step 2, printed p.151, componentwise refinement of the prime-to-ell alteration in diagram (2.c). Agent-extracted clopen-selection, closed-graph and closed-image arguments of returned item steps 10--12. Normal components are clopen by Stacks properties.tex Tag 033M (lemma-normal-Noetherian); projectivity over B uses the graph over the separated e-scheme B.

proof.text: The structure morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ is proper by [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper], hence of finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. The one-point scheme $\operatorname{Spec}F$ is Noetherian: its affine coordinate ring has only the ideals $0,F$, so its single affine chart is Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth], and its one-point space is quasi-compact. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $X$ Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 01T6, lemma-finite-type-noetherian; projective properness as in Tag 01WC, lemma-locally-projective-proper.

proof.text: By clause (2) of [rem-pc-regular-normal], normality and Noetherianness make the irreducible components of $X$ a finite disjoint family of clopen normal integral open subschemes. The selected components and the omitted components are each unions of members of this family, so their complementary unions are open; hence $X^\circ$ is clopen. Its local rings are those of $X$, so it is normal. The inclusion $j:X^\circ\hookrightarrow X$ is also a closed immersion by [def-weil-closed-immersion]: it identifies a closed subset, and the structure-sheaf map is locally the identity on $X^\circ$ and the map to the zero sheaf on its open complement, hence surjective. Here the open structure is exactly the restricted structure sheaf of [def-weil-open-immersion].

source.place: Tag 033M, lemma-normal-Noetherian; the subsequent clopen inclusion check is direct from the definitions.

proof.text: Choose a closed immersion $i:X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_F$ witnessing the hypothesis [def-kun-projective]. Since $j$ is a closed immersion, [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-comp] makes $i\circ j:X^\circ\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_F$ a closed immersion. It witnesses projectivity of $X^\circ$ over $F$ in the required finite-projective-space convention.

source.place: Tag 01QS, lemma-composition-closed-immersion, applied to the chosen projective embedding.

proof.text: The irreducible components of $X^\circ$ are precisely the selected components: an irreducible subset cannot meet two complementary clopen unions, and maximality then reduces to maximality inside a single selected component [def-weil-irreducible-components]. Each such component has exactly one generic point by [lem-sc-scheme-sober]. Its chosen $c_b$ remains generic because its closure in the open subspace is the same component. Thus the generic points of $X^\circ$ are exactly the chosen $c_b$, with repetitions discarded, and each fibre over a generic $b$ contains its $c_b$.

source.place: Tag 01IS, lemma-scheme-sober; the component comparison is a direct clopen-subspace argument.

proof.text: At any selected $c_b$, restriction to the open subscheme gives $\mathcal O_{X^\circ,c_b}=\mathcal O_{X,c_b}$: neighbourhoods contained in $X^\circ$ are cofinal among neighbourhoods of $c_b$ [def-weil-open-immersion]. Taking the quotients by the same maximal ideal identifies the residue fields and identifies the maps induced by $d|_{X^\circ}$ and $d$ [def-weil-residue-field]. Consequently every generic point found in step 4 maps to its generic $b$ with exactly the assumed finite degree prime to $\ell$. No assertion uses the omitted components.

source.place: Open subscheme restriction of the structure sheaf; elementary stalk and residue-field calculation.

proof.text: Because $B$ is proper over $e$, it is separated over $e$ [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-constant-projective-graph] with $k=e$, $R=X^\circ$, $S=B$, and $c=d|_{X^\circ}$. Its hypotheses hold by step 3 and the given finite extension $F/e$. Taking the identity $B\to B$ and the identity base change gives a finite-projective-space closed embedding over $B$, and makes $d|_{X^\circ}$ proper and projective in both projectivity conventions.

source.place: Tag 0C4Q, lemma-projective-permanence, with the finite-constant extension graph lemma and its stated identity base change.

proof.text: The image $C=d(X^\circ)$ is closed in $B$ by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-closed-image], since step 6 proves properness. Every integral summand of $B$ is irreducible [def-pc-integral-scheme] and, being clopen in the given finite disjoint union, is an irreducible component of $B$. It has a generic point $b$ by [lem-sc-scheme-sober]. Step 4 puts $b$ in $C$. By [def-sc-generic-point], the closure of $b$ is that entire summand; closedness of $C$ therefore puts every summand in $C$. They cover $B$, so $C=B$ and the restricted morphism is surjective.

source.place: Tag 01W6, lemma-image-proper-scheme-closed; closure of each generic point gives surjectivity.
